meta.title: LEGO Was $800M In Debt And Months From Bankruptcy
meta.hook: In 2003, LEGO was $800 million in debt and months from bankruptcy.
meta.description: By 2003 LEGO had expanded into theme parks, clothing lines and video games, lost nearly $300 million that year, and had $800 million in debt with sales down 30% over two years. New CEO Jorgen Vig Knudstorp diagnosed the problem as too little focus, not too little innovation — selling the theme parks and cutting the product catalog from 13,000 parts to about 7,000. By 2015, LEGO had passed Mattel as the world's most profitable toy company.

scenes.narration: In two thousand three, LEGO was eight hundred million dollars in debt and months from bankruptcy.

visual.query: colorful building blocks toy pieces close up
visual.visual_intent: Colorful plastic building blocks scattered on a table, macro close focus
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: figure corroborated by multiple business-turnaround analyses (Art of the Brand, The Strategy Institute)

scenes.narration: It wasn't a toy problem. LEGO had turned itself into a sprawling company: theme parks, clothing lines, video games, all at once.

visual.visual_intent: A theme park rollercoaster track against the sky, wide establishing shot
visual.decision_reason: LEGOLAND theme park diversification, corroborated by multiple turnaround case studies

scenes.narration: That same year the company lost nearly three hundred million dollars, and sales had fallen thirty percent over two years.

visual.query: financial chart declining bars red screen
visual.visual_intent: A declining bar chart on a dark financial screen, red emphasis on the drop
visual.decision_reason: 2003 loss ~$300M and 30% sales drop over two years, per business-turnaround case analyses

scenes.narration: In two thousand four, new CEO Jorgen Vig Knudstorp made a blunt diagnosis: the problem wasn't too little innovation. It was too little focus.

visual.visual_intent: A serious executive presenting at a boardroom table, focused corporate light
visual.decision_reason: Jorgen Vig Knudstorp became CEO in 2004, corroborated across multiple sources

scenes.narration: He sold the theme parks, cut the clothing lines, and slashed the product catalog from thirteen thousand parts down to about seven thousand.

visual.visual_intent: Warehouse shelving with product boxes being sorted or reduced, industrial light
visual.decision_reason: SKU cut from 13,000 to 7,000, corroborated by multiple turnaround case studies

scenes.narration: By twenty fifteen, LEGO had passed Mattel to become the world's most profitable toy company, built by making fewer things. Follow for more.

visual.visual_intent: A completed colorful block structure, satisfying final composition, bright light
visual.decision_reason: closing takeaway; 2015 milestone corroborated by multiple business press retrospectives
